title: Reaching the Limits of Ground-State Metrology with Many-Body Probes
summary: We investigate the physical requirements to reach the ultimate limits of ground-state metrology -- i.e., the estimation of an unknown parameter $θ$ of an $N$-body Hamiltonian via measurements on its ground state -- using many-body probes featuring either short-range or long-range interactions. We characterize the conditions to saturate two fundamental limits of the quantum Fisher information $F_θ$: the static ground-state bound $F_θ\lesssim N^2/Δ^2$, where $Δ$ is the spectral gap, and the dynamical Heisenberg limit $F_θ\lesssim N^2 τ^2$, where $τ$ is the total protocol duration.
